title: Solo features 'Stardust' and 'Body and Soul'; no recordings
summary: He was the featured soloist in each band; neither Sissle's nor Harlan Leonard's band recorded in his time.

blocks.x: You said that Noble was interested in you. He claimed he needed an attraction. Did he have special solo duties that he wanted you to do?
Yes, I always did solo work like I did with Louie, and most of the time --
Well "Stardust" was one of my songs.

Yeah, "Stardust" and "Body and Soul." Different....I wasn't singing then. That's what I did with the Jeter-Pillars band as I did with Armstrong and I was featured--they would call me down and I'd play in front of the band. Do my little solo. It was nice.
Noble Sissle orchestra never recorded at that time?
No, he didn't do any recording.
Did any of the other bands you were in before then, did they record, say, Harlan Leonard didn't record at the time you were with him?
No, they didn't record. Ernie was with him. Fields didn't record while I, They recorded before I got in.
So the Jeter-Pillars orchestra was the transition between Noble Sissle and Louis Armstrong.
